items.title: Bitcoin Fork Rally Driven by CME Futures Listing
points: CME Group announced Bitcoin Cash futures (contracts letting traders bet on future price without owning the asset) launching October 19, pending regulatory approval.
Bitcoin Cash (BCH) surged 60% this week and Bitcoin SV jumped 40%, both riding institutional interest sparked by the CME news.
This mirrors historical patterns where Bitcoin forks temporarily outpace the parent coin during speculative surges.
Bitcoin itself pulled back from a seven-month high above $87,000 to $84,033, down 2.4% in 24 hours.

items.title: Decade-Old Bitcoin Wallets Reactivating at Scale
points: $161 million in Bitcoin held in wallets dormant for roughly 10 years moved in just the past two weeks.
The reawakening shows no signs of slowing, suggesting steady activity from early adopters.
Timing coincides with Bitcoin's recent price surge putting long-term holders back into profit for the first time in years.

items.title: Security Threat: North Korean Job Scam Targets Crypto Holders
points: A seven-agency advisory linked the WaterPlum hacking crew and North Korea's remote IT worker scheme to the same government bureau.
Fake job interviews drained $11 million from about 7,000 crypto wallets.
The operation shows a sophisticated social engineering approach targeting cryptocurrency holders.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF Inflows and Other Notes
points: Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that let investors gain BTC exposure through regular brokerage accounts) saw nearly $1 billion in net inflows Monday as the price surge returned average holders to profit.

items.title: CFTC's Pivot to 24/7 Market Regulation
points: CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the US regulator overseeing derivatives markets) Chair Mike Selig said the agency is developing oversight frameworks for markets that trade 24/7 rather than fixed hours.
The move follows the failure of the Clarity Act, a proposed law meant to give crypto and AI asset markets a dedicated legislative framework.
On-chain markets (trading that happens directly on blockchain networks) run continuously across global time zones, unlike traditional exchanges, requiring new regulatory approaches.

headlines: CFTC Chair Mike Selig signals the regulator is preparing oversight frameworks for 24/7 crypto and AI markets, shifting strategy after the Clarity Act legislative effort failed
On-chain trading markets operating continuously across all time zones will require new regulatory approaches from traditional market regulators
Failure of the Clarity Act leaves crypto markets without comprehensive federal legislation, forcing regulators to adapt existing frameworks

sections.title: CFTC's Pivot to 24/7 Market Regulation
points: Chair Mike Selig announced the CFTC is developing regulatory structures for markets that operate around-the-clock rather than traditional trading hours
The move follows the Clarity Act's failure to pass, eliminating the possibility of dedicated legislative framework for crypto and AI asset markets
On-chain markets operate continuously across global time zones, unlike traditional exchanges with defined trading hours, requiring fundamentally different oversight approaches
